description: CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became. LS-DATE='BC220719  ' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='<BC>YYMMDD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. This program opens no file and is reached by no JCL, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and takes no job parameter - its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 and the group move at L122, never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible here. Arm 5 by a second route: a SUPPORTED era name that places the date before the common era and therefore far below the Lillian epoch. Paired with case09 this proves the era field is genuinely decoded rather than merely skipped - 'BC' is accepted as a name and then rejected on range, where 'XX' is rejected as a name - and the two land on different arms.
